gates.title: The agent can move fast. The gates stop it from confidently breaking things.
gates.description: A gate is just a deterministic check with permission to say “no.” It does not care how persuasive the AI sounds. If the code, ownership, data rules, or build do not agree, the change stays red.

items.label: 01 / PREFLIGHT
items.question: Are we safe to start?
items.description: Checks the release, Node version, Git state, host, dependencies, and provider mode before anything is written.
items.catches: Wrong environment, dirty work, missing baseline, and unsafe live-provider assumptions.

items.label: 02 / OWNERSHIP
items.question: Does this feature have one clear home?
items.description: Looks up which system owns the responsibility, table, route, and lifecycle so the agent extends the existing authority.
items.catches: Duplicate subsystems, two tables for the same noun, and business logic scattered across routes.

items.label: 03 / CONTRACTS
items.question: Do all the pieces agree?
items.description: Regenerates typed contracts so the backend, web app, API, CLI, and MCP expose the same operation and failures.
items.catches: UI/backend drift, hand-edited generated files, missing error cases, and broken headless surfaces.

items.label: 04 / FOCUSED PROOF
items.question: Did this exact change actually work?
items.description: Runs the smallest relevant set of formatting, types, tests, builds, schema, topology, security, and route checks.
items.catches: Code that compiles but breaks a route, a migration, tenancy, a provider boundary, or another package.

items.label: 05 / RECEIPT
items.question: Can another human verify what happened?
items.description: Keeps the approved fingerprints, generated-file provenance, transaction journal, and verification result with the change.
items.catches: Mystery edits, unverifiable AI claims, and “it worked on my machine” handoffs.

You only need a static marketing page or the quickest possible throwaway mockup.

faqs.question: Is this a course or the actual codebase?
faqs.answer: It is the actual template codebase, plus the architecture guides, generators, quality gates, and delivery receipts used to work with it. You can inspect and change everything in your copy.

faqs.question: Do I need to know Convex, Effect, or Confect first?
faqs.answer: No. You can start from the working reference patterns and let your coding agent follow the repo instructions. The deeper architecture is there when your app needs stronger contracts, workflows, and failure handling.

faqs.question: Do I need to be a developer?
faqs.answer: You do not need to be a senior engineer or know this stack already. You do need to be comfortable working in Claude Code or Codex, using a terminal and Git, reviewing a plan or diff, and asking the agent to fix red checks. This is agent-assisted coding, not no-code.

faqs.question: Does it include live authentication and billing?
faqs.answer: It includes provider-shaped seams and fake-safe local adapters. You choose and connect the live auth, billing, email, analytics, storage, and LLM providers for each product instead of inheriting somebody else’s production accounts.

faqs.question: Which coding agents can I use?
faqs.answer: The template is designed for repo-aware agents such as Codex and Claude Code. Its instructions, architecture maps, generators, and gates live with the code, so the workflow is not tied to one chat session.

faqs.question: What can I build with it?
faqs.answer: AI workflow products, vertical SaaS apps, client portals, internal operations tools, agent systems, and other products that need real tenancy, typed data, durable work, and a polished application shell.

faqs.question: Why is the launch price only $29?
faqs.answer: This is the low-ticket builder launch. The goal is to get the template into the hands of people who will use it on real products, learn what they reach for first, and improve the package quickly.

faqs.question: What if it is too much for my project?
faqs.answer: Use only the layers you need. The live surface is deliberately thin, providers are swappable, and the docs distinguish real production paths from contract fixtures. You are buying a strong starting point, not a requirement to activate everything.
